evals.title: Overview and core concepts of architecture generations
evals.prompt: Please introduce the architectural generation division of Ascend NPU, including the meaning and relationship of the core concepts of NpuArch, SocVersion, __NPU_ARCH__, and archXX.
evals.expected_output:
The reply should explain the core concepts of the Ascend NPU architecture:
- NpuArch: chip architecture number, defines the instruction set and microarchitecture, obtained through GetCurNpuArch() at runtime
- SocVersion: system on chip version, software naming identifier, obtained through GetSocVersion() at runtime
- __NPU_ARCH__: Device side compilation macro, four-digit value, used for conditional compilation
- archXX: abbreviation of operator warehouse directory, take the first two digits of the DAV number (such as DAV_2201 → arch22, DAV_3510 → arch35)
- One-to-many relationship: one NpuArch can correspond to multiple SocVersion (such as DAV_2201 corresponds to Ascend910B1~B4, Ascend910B2C, Ascend910_93)

evals.title: DAV_3510 vs DAV_2201 Key Differences
evals.prompt: What are the key changes in Buffer capacity, instruction set and data path between DAV_3510 and DAV_2201?
evals.expected_output:
Reply should cover key changes of DAV_3510:
- Buffer capacity: L0C 128→256 KB, UB 192→248 KB, BT 1→4 KB
- Data format: Added FP8/MXFP8/MXFP4/HiF8 Cube MMAD
- CV pass-through: Added L0C→UB, UB→L1, SSBuffer Message channel to avoid GM workspace transfer
- Synchronization mechanism: BufferID replaces set/wait strong pairing to simplify multi-pipeline operator synchronization
- Sparse support: DAV_3510 no longer supports 4:2 sparse matrix calculation

evals.title: SIMT vs SIMD architectural differences
evals.prompt: What is the difference between SIMT and SIMD programming models in Ascend C? What scenarios are they suitable for?
evals.expected_output:
Reply should compare the core differences between SIMT and SIMD:
- SIMT: scalar programming (thread perspective), Warp scheduling (32 thread grouping), 4 Warp Schedulers per AIV
- SIMD: vector programming (continuous calculation within VF), software unrolled loops
- SIMT applicable scenarios: Gather/Scatter, Hash insertion, random number, sorting (including atomic operations)
- SIMD applicable scenarios: large blocks dense BF16/FP16 matrix multiplication/convolution, long vector sequential calculation
- SIMT is only supported by DAV_3510, the previous generation architecture cannot be used
- SIMT unique hardware: DCache (maximum 128KB, reuse UB as Cacheline), supports GM discrete access

evals.title: Derivation of computing power formula
evals.prompt: What are the computing power of Cube BF16 and FP8 of Ascend950PR Server? How are they derived?
evals.expected_output:
The reply should give the computing power derivation formula and calculation process:
- Cube BF16 computing power formula: TFLOPS = M × K × N × Number of cores × freq(MHz) × 2 ÷ 10^6
- Cube MAC array of BF16/FP16: M×K×N = 16×16×16 = 4096
- 950PR Server BF16: 4096 × 32 × 1650 × 2 ÷ 10^6 = 432 TFLOPS
- FP8’s Cube MAC array is larger: M×K×N = 16×32×16 = 8192
- 950PR Server FP8: 8192 × 32 × 1650 × 2 ÷ 10^6 = 865 TFLOPS
- Vector computing power formula: TFLOPS = vec_calc_size × vector_core_cnt × vec_freq(MHz) × 2 ÷ 10^6

evals.title: UB capacity caliber (512KB vs 248KB)
evals.prompt: Table 4-2 of the Ascend 950 white paper writes that UB is 512KB per AI Core, but GetCoreMemSize returns 248KB. Are these two values contradictory? Which one should be used when tiling?
evals.expected_output:
The reply should explain the UB capacity caliber:
- No contradiction: 512KB in the white paper table 4-2 is the physical capacity calculated by AI Core group (1 AIC + 2 AIV), that is, 256KB × 2 per AIV. 
- 248KB (INI ub_size=253952) is the available value per AIV user, that is, physical 256KB − 8KB reserved
- Conclusion: Single AIV physical 256KB / available 248KB, group-level physical 512KB
- Tiling is always based on the return value of GetCoreMemSize(CoreMemType::UB), hard coding is prohibited

evals.title: NDDMA and BufferID mechanism details
evals.prompt: What capabilities does the NDDMA instruction of DAV_3510 have? What changes does the BufferID synchronization mechanism have compared to set/wait?
evals.expected_output:
The reply should explain NDDMA and BufferID (Ascend 950 NPU Architecture White Paper §4.1.5/§4.1.6):
- NDDMA: Rearrange global memory data in up to 5 dimensions and write it directly to UB. The transfer and rearrangement/transposition are completed in one step; the built-in cache automatically explores data locality and merges reads of multiple data element granularities into 128-byte reads
- BufferID: replacement set/wait forces pairing, get_buf() corresponds to locking, rel_buf() corresponds to unlocking, similar to mutex lock semantics, stronger cohesion, and decoupled from other pipelines
